newsitem.title: UK: U.S. is biggest direct investor in UK in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: U.S. is biggest direct investor in UK in 1996/97.

text.p: The United States accounted for 240 of the 483 foreign direct investment projects notified to the government's Invest in Britain Bureau in 1996/97, according to the bureau's annual report released on Wednesday.

U.S. companies ploughed 3.99 billion pounds into Britain, more than 40 percent of the investment total of 9.35 billion pounds. The biggest single investment was Ford Motor Co's 2.6 billion stg modernisation of car plants in England and Wales.
Korea was the second-biggest source of direct investment, with 2.70 billion stg, followed by Japan with 884 million stg and Germany on 784 million stg, the report showed.
It said Britain remained the second largest recipient of inward investment in the developed world after the United States.
It continued to attract more than 40 percent of U.S. and Japanese investment in the European Union and was also the most popular venue for cross-border investment from other EU states.
In all, the stock of foreign direct investment in Britain is estimated to have reached nearly 160 billion stg, the report said, without giving comparative figures.
